newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Further Italy rate cut seen before summer.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Further Italy rate cut seen before summer.

text.p: Italy's central bank, following its surprise 75 basis point interest rate cut, could shave a further 50 to 75 bps off official rates before the end of June, a Reuter poll of 12 analysts showed on Wednesday.

The Bank of Italy announced on Tuesday night it was cutting the official discount rate to 6.75 percent from 7.50 percent and the fixed-term advances, or Lombard rate, to 8.25 percent from 9.00 percent, both effective from Wednesday.

Analysts' optimism was based on expectations of a further fall in Italian consumer price inflation, the fairly speedy approval of a supplementary "mini-budget" and a positive global economic scenario.

Worries of inflation linked to labour costs appeared to have been put aside. The fact the Bank cut its rates before an accord has been reached between metalworkers and employers in a long-running pay dispute, the analysts said, was a sign that a non-inflationary solution was imminent.
"Inflation will continue to fall moderately until the end of March. Then I expect to see a major drop to perhaps 1.7 percent by end-June," said Martino Dolfini of Chase Manhattan Bank.
Other analysts, slightly less optimistic, saw year on year CPI of 2.0/2.1 percent in June.

The central bank's reduction followed preliminary CPI data from 11 Italian cities which pointed to consumer prices rising 2.6 percent year on year in January, unchanged from the previous two months and slightly better than expected.
The Bank wants to see average inflation this year below 3.0 percent from 3.9 percent in 1996, the government's target. The government's 1997 goal is for average inflation of 2.5 percent.
"I think the timing of the next cut, seen around March/April, will be determined by the mini-budget or at least some decision on putting state finances in order," Dolfini said.
He added that aside from a 75 bp cut all at once, he did not exclude the possibility of more frequent reductions of a smaller size. "But by end-June we should be at 6.0 percent or below."

Fabio Stolfa of brokers Caboto, who saw Tuesday's cut as "necessary and not excessive" given monetary easing elsewhere in Europe, agreed that there would be another reduction in April "due entirely to a new fall in inflation."
Roberto Fumagalli of J.P.Morgan also cited the international situation as favouring further Italian rate cuts.

"The U.S. scenario indicates renewed dollar strength following a Federal Reserve hike, possibly sometime from the March FOMC meeting onwards, while on the other hand the macroeconomic situation in Germany suggests a repo rate reduction is possible."
Also favouring further Italian cuts is the performance of the lira, said Francesco Giordano of San Paolo Bank.

"The lira is stronger than it would have been if the recovery in France and Germany had been more lively. Against the mark the lira is near its 2.25 percent informal limit, with respect to the EMS central parity, and the Bank of Italy is not too happy with these levels," he said.
The lira, which firmed to a new high against the mark of 966.45 on January 20, was trading on Wednesday around 971.
Following are results of the poll:
1. Will the Bank of Italy's next move on rates be to cut?
2. When?
By April 3/12
By the end of the second quarter 9/12
3. By how much?
Note: Taking part in the poll were: Banca di Roma, Banco di Sardegna, Caboto, Cariplo, Credit Italiano, Chase Manhattan Bank, Deutsche Bank, HSBC, J.P.Morgan, NatWest, San Paolo Bank, UBS.
